lines.x: If you don't mind, try this test build of the fully automated file archiving system. Absolutely efficient, absolutely reliable. Yes, that's right—I'd have to rebuild your entire bookshelf and archive, but it won't take long. Hm, you'd still rather keep things the way they are? Understood.

That's my task list. I don't often get the chance to follow it strictly, but having one never hurts. At the very least it separates my project stages, so I don't end up embedding a weapon bearing into something while running the crane in the assembly plant.

Sorry, give me a few more seconds. The sobering pills haven't kicked in yet... I know, I'll be more careful next time—so, what do you need me for, Doctor? The new standard-issue weapon selection, the Rhodes Island construction progress meeting, or the heavy machinery import negotiations?

The Vector Breakthrough assessment data is already back at the workshop. I flagged a number of holes—patch them and both the carried equipment and the Structural Principle will hold up more reliably in extreme conditions. By the way, did you have fun during the test, Doctor?

You may find it hard to imagine a creation being worth more than its creator, but that is exactly how Volvort Kochinski weighs it. Run it through an 'asset recombination' and the invention has nothing to do with the inventor anymore. I'm glad that logic doesn't hold at Rhodes Island.

Without Whitesmith, I might really have left Rhodes Island and gone back to Columbia. You should be able to understand it—that brilliance technology has once you strip the sentiment away. She left the workshop to me, so I'm still here, commemorating her with every gleam that rises off the steel.

Maybe I don't count as a pure technology fanatic either. I was willing to dress myself up, work the cocktail circuit, take public speaking lessons, learn to hunt—all to win over investors... Does that make me well-rounded? All right, then I'll accept the compliment.

Banshee incantations are actually a kind of technical terminology. Set aside a few prejudices about the occult and they're not hard to learn. Oh—you do need a good Banshee for a teacher. Ha, don't let Logos's usual manner fool you; he's an excellent instructor. Want me to bring you along to a lesson next time?

Every stack of Originium and steel at Rhodes Island points toward a single goal. I don't know when all this expenditure will finally stop the stone on the back of my hand from spreading, but the advance of technology will answer that question in the future. I'm glad I get to leave a footnote of my own on that answer.
Something to drink, to oil the brain?

Authorization code acquired... Cross-check clean... All right, that'll do. I'll handle the rest of the transfer paperwork in one batch. Rhodes Island Elite Operator Mechanist, entering your chain of command as of today.
I've already got a line on the improvements. Let's talk it over in a bit.
The medal may have been made by my own hands, but your trust is irreplaceable, Doctor.
With your leadership, I believe that one day we will break the shackles Originium has placed on technology.
Equipment online.
Connected to the command hub. Everyone, confirm the briefing.
Checking the equipment again.
Commencing operation.
Ready.
Equipment prepped.
Structural Principle, ready to deploy.
Weapon safety off.
Protocol One, suppressive fire.
Protocol Two, artillery defense.
Protocol Three, eradicate the threat.
Protocol Four, 'Mechanical Dawn.'
Hah. Looks like my model needs another upgrade.
The numbers broadly match our pre-battle estimates. Good work.
The data fluctuation is still within acceptable range.
Initiating the contingency plan. Time to leave, Doctor.
Work is the same wherever I do it.
I just got my helmet adjusted comfortably...
Let me borrow your terminal—there's some data I don't have clearance for.
Arknights.

It's the New Year already?! Hah, once I get busy I forget everything. Come on, Doctor, we should go celebrate with everyone. I'll skip the alcohol this time. Some moments are better sober—you remember them more clearly that way.
You're looking well, Doctor.

I've always wanted to know—was the calendar your birth was reckoned by the same one we use? And if it was, is that coincidence, or some kind of inheritance? Ah, it's just curiosity. I know you don't have the answer. Here—cheers. Happy birthday.

Time is like Originium—we forever lament having too little, yet fear receiving more. When will we finally forge the scale that can bear them, so those problems leave this land for good? Heh, I know. That's your subject. Just remember—if you run into trouble, come find us.
